steps.notes: Signature OK (lanczos(A,b,m) matches all 3 test calls); spec complete enough for a competent solver (q1=b/||b|| implied by input b + 'orthonormal columns'); tests 2 and 3 pass with every correct variant tried; test 1 fails ALL of them due to exact Lanczos breakdown (see findings). Cosmetic only: description text omits input b ('takes a symmetric matrix A a number of iterations m') and misspells 'orthonomal' -- header/problem_io fully define b, so not score-affecting.

findings.evidence: Test case 1 (A = tridiag(-1/h, 2/h, -1/h), n=7, h=1/7; b=[0.1,0.1,0.0,0.1,0.0,0.1,0.1]; m=5) suffers EXACT Lanczos breakdown: b is palindromic and A is centro-symmetric, so the Krylov subspace K(A,b) has dimension exactly 4 (numpy matrix_rank of [b, Ab, ..., A^6 b] = 4; singular values drop from 3.3e-1 to 1.3e-10). Running standard Lanczos gives beta_4 = 1.083e-14 (machine-noise zero), yet m=5 requires 6 orthonormal columns. Columns 5 and 6 of the frozen target are therefore pure floating-point roundoff of whatever implementation generated it. Verified dynamically: 8 distinct mathematically-correct implementations (Trefethen&Bau Alg 36.1 ordering, Paige/Golub-Van-Loan ordering, alpha-subtracted-first ordering, alpha as quadratic form, np.dot variant, Arnoldi-style modified GS, Arnoldi-style classical GS, full reorthogonalization x2) ALL reproduce target columns 1-4 to 0.0 but differ from target columns 5-6 by per-column max|diff| between 0.68 and 1.23 -- each variant produces a DIFFERENT noise direction. steptest result for every variant: 'RESULT step 5.1: 2/3 tests pass' with test 1 AssertionError. Since the official scorer requires all 3 tests, no solver passes step 5.1 (the problem's only step) unless its arithmetic order bit-matches the reference. The prompt also gives no breakdown-handling rule (D4 facet), but no rule could fix it: the post-breakdown columns are mathematically undefined.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace test 1's starting vector with any non-palindromic b (e.g. b=[0.1,0.2,0.0,0.1,0.0,0.3,0.1], which breaks the centro-symmetry so Krylov grade >= 6) OR reduce m to 3, then regenerate the h5 target. Alternatively drop test 1; tests 2 and 3 are well-conditioned (all beta in [4.5, 90]) and already constrain the implementation.

findings.evidence: Same root cause as the D6 finding, but independently provable from the h5 file alone: the frozen target for test 1 violates the spec's own output contract. Prompt: 'outputs a new matrix Q with orthonomal columns'. The (7,6) target has unit-norm columns but max |Q^T Q - I| = 0.945: q4.q5 = 0.945 and q3.q6 = 0.916, i.e. the last two target columns are nearly parallel to earlier ones. A grader checking the documented property would reject the target itself. Targets for tests 2 and 3 are orthonormal to 1e-8 and consistent with the spec.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate the test-1 target after fixing the degenerate input (see D6 fix); any regenerated target should satisfy ||Q^T Q - I|| < 1e-10 as a sanity gate.

overall_assessment: Problem 5 is a clean one-step Lanczos task with a matching signature and an inferable spec, and 2 of 3 frozen tests are sound. However test 1's input lies exactly on a Lanczos breakdown (Krylov grade 4 < m+1 = 6), so the last two target columns encode one implementation's roundoff noise; eight distinct correct implementations all fail it with O(1) errors while passing tests 2-3. Because the harness requires all test cases of the step, the problem as shipped scores essentially every competent solver as 0. Not fair to score as-is; fixing or dropping test 1 makes it fair.
